title: Dispatching an Exit State
statement: Let $k>0$, let $S$ be a finite type with decidable equality, and let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine over Boolean symbols and states $S$. Choose a starting state $s$, and an injective map $e$ from optional Boolean values to $S$. Then there are a finite state type $R$ with decidable equality, a $k$-work-tape machine $N$ over Boolean symbols and states $R$, an entry state in $R$, and an injective map $\ell$ from bits to $R$ with the following property. For any Boolean input $x$, time $t$, and optional bit $v$, suppose the run of $M$ from the configuration with state $s$ and empty work tapes reaches state $e(v)$ at time $t$, and does not reach any state $e(q)$ at any earlier time. Then the run of $N$ from its entry state with empty work tapes, on input $x$, reaches at time $t+1$ the configuration obtained from that run of $M$ by replacing its state with $\ell(1)$ when $v$ is the present bit $1$, and with $\ell(0)$ otherwise. Moreover, before or at time $t+1$, the run of $N$ never reaches any state in the image of $\ell$.
